note: Starter examples only, not a complete rule library. Version date is the effective date of the rule text this file was checked against. Local rules, court orders, and stipulations can change any of these periods; verify before relying on a computed date.

rules.summary: A defendant must serve an answer within 21 days after being served with the summons and complaint.
rules.title: Answer after service of summons and complaint
rules.trigger: being served with the summons and complaint

rules.summary: A defendant that waived service must serve an answer within 60 days after the request for a waiver was sent (90 days if the request was sent outside a judicial district of the United States; that variant is not encoded here and must be checked by hand).
rules.title: Answer after waiving service
rules.trigger: the request for waiver was sent (defendant waived service)

rules.summary: The responding party must serve its answers and any objections within 30 days after being served with the interrogatories.
rules.title: Answers and objections to interrogatories

rules.summary: The party to whom a request for production is directed must respond in writing within 30 days after being served.
rules.title: Response to requests for production
rules.trigger: being served with requests for production

rules.summary: A matter is admitted unless, within 30 days after being served, the party to whom the request is directed serves a written answer or objection.
rules.title: Response to requests for admission
rules.trigger: being served with requests for admission

rules.summary: A motion for a new trial must be filed no later than 28 days after the entry of judgment. Rule 6(b)(2) bars extending this time, and Rule 6(d) does not apply because the period runs from entry of judgment, not from service.
rules.title: Motion for a new trial

source: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, published by the U.S. Courts (uscourts.gov)
